questions.prompt: You wrote a review subagent and it has never once been picked, even when you say "review this" by name. Where is the bug most likely?
options: The Markdown body is too long, so Claude can't get to the decision
The tools list is missing Read and Grep, so Claude assumes it can't review anything
The description says what the agent does but never says when to use it
The name is kebab-case; Claude only routes to snake_case names
questions.explanation: Routing happens on the description alone, before the body is ever read — so a description that only says what the agent does gives Claude no reason to choose it. Body length and tool list are invisible at routing time, and name casing is irrelevant: identity comes from the name field, not from a naming convention.

questions.prompt: An agent must read the whole repo and report findings, and must never be able to change anything. Which frontmatter is correct?
options: A body that opens with "You are read-only. Never edit files."
questions.explanation: An allowlist is the strongest form here: Edit and Write are not in the pool, so they are not callable at all. A denylist is weaker — it removes two tools from a pool that can also gain new ones as Claude Code ships. Option C is a request, not a restriction; the model can comply or not. Option D changes how prompts surface, not which tools exist, so Bash could still write.

questions.prompt: You add permissionMode: maxTurns to a subagent and it keeps running forever. What is actually happening?
options: maxTurns is a valid field but must be lowercase
maxTurns is silently ignored because you wrote it outside the tools field
maxTurns is silently ignored because the field name is max_turns
maxTurns only applies to background subagents, and yours runs in the foreground
questions.explanation: Unrecognized frontmatter fields are ignored with no warning at all — the field is maxTurns in camelCase, and max_turns isn't a field, so your cap never applied and the agent ran unbounded. Option B misplaces the issue: frontmatter fields all sit in the same block. Option D is wrong because the cap applies regardless of foreground or background.

questions.prompt: You have .claude/agents/notes.md and .claude/agents/research/notes.md, both with name: notes, and you start Claude from the repo root. Which definition is live?
options: Neither — duplicate names are rejected at startup
The one in .claude/agents/, because shallower always wins
The one in .claude/agents/research/, because it is nested and therefore more specific
Whichever file git tracked most recently
questions.explanation: For duplicate names in nested project scopes, the definition closest to the working directory wins — research/ is closer to where you're standing than the agents/ root. There is no rejection and no git ordering; option B invents a depth rule that doesn't exist.
